title: A Gravity for the Echo
premise: Mirabel Thornbury has spent eleven years alone tending the Halcyon Seed Vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony fleet that stopped answering. When a ghost ship's manifest lists a passenger who shouldn't exist—her own name, dated forty years in the future—she discovers the vault is a node in a buried justice network: evidence of the fleet government's deliberate abandonment of the colonies, hidden in the seed genomes themselves. Pursued by a truce-bound salvage crew ordered to erase the vault, Mirabel and the ship's estranged pilot, Dario Voss, race across dead space to reach the last functioning relay and broadcast the inheritance before the truce expires and the fleet's silence becomes permanent. They succeed at terrible cost: Dario stays behind to hold the relay open as it burns, and Mirabel, carrying the truth home, must decide whether justice delivered this way can ever feel like survival.
about_author: Cyrus Pemberton is the pen name of a former agricultural archivist who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom seed collections before turning to fiction. Their work explores how ordinary custodianship becomes extraordinary when institutions fail.

chapters.title: The Quiet Inventory
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She walks the vault's frozen corridors, logging germination tests on seeds that will never be planted, and records her 4,000th daily broadcast into silence. The emotional beat is ritualized loneliness—competence as a shield against grief.

chapters.title: A Name That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A derelict freighter docks unbidden; its manifest updates itself, listing 'M. Thornbury' with a date decades ahead. She finds the ship empty except for one cryopod, cold and long vacant. Beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Quit Flying
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. The pod's emergency beacon wakes Dario Voss, the ship's sole crewman, who fled the fleet after refusing an order he still won't name. He recognizes the manifest anomaly—and knows exactly who will come looking. Beat: guilt wearing pragmatism.

chapters.title: Terms of Salvage
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A salvage crew under Captain Ondine Reyes arrives claiming the freighter under truce law. Mirabel hides in the vault's deep archive while Dario negotiates, buying time but learning the crew carries sealed orders from Fleet Command. Beat: the first lie told face-to-face.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Decoding the anomalous genome tags, she finds encrypted testimony embedded in seed lineages: logs proving the fleet cut off the colonies deliberately, then burned the records. Her predecessor built the archive as a court that never convened. Beat: revelation as vertigo.

chapters.title: The Order Sealed in Wax
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. We see the salvage crew's true mission: sterilize the vault, recover the genome keys, leave no witnesses. Reyes hesitates—her brother was born on an abandoned colony. Beat: complicity cracking along old wounds.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Weather
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, flashback-woven. How she came to the vault fleeing her own family's role in the abandonment, and why she stayed when everyone left. Beat: understanding that she chose exile before she was sentenced to it.

chapters.title: Running on Dead Engines
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. He and Mirabel steal the freighter out of dock during a debris storm, engines failing, navigation blind. The escape works only because Dario finally confesses his refused order: he was meant to deliver the sterilization command years ago. Beat: confession as lifeline.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The fleet grants the salvage crew seventy-two hours before the inter-fleet truce expires and open retrieval—meaning violence—becomes legal. Reyes must choose between her orders and the growing suspicion her crew will be erased too. Beat: the hunter realizing she is also prey.

chapters.title: Waystation of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At a drifting colony ruin, they find survivors' graffiti and a child's shoe fused to the deck—physical proof matching the genome testimony. Mirabel breaks down; Dario holds the watch alone. Beat: grief given a body.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. They intercept a repeating transmission—the same manifest anomaly, now listing Reyes's name too. The network is recruiting witnesses, or marking them. Trust between Mirabel and Dario frays over what the inheritance demands of them. Beat: paranoia inside intimacy.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. First sight of the ancient relay station, half-swallowed by a nebula, its antenna still turning toward a fleet that no longer listens. Powering it requires a human operator in the exposed core ring. Beat: awe curdling into arithmetic—who pays.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes the Distance
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The salvage ship corners them at the relay. Instead of firing, Reyes boards alone and asks to read the testimony. What she reads confirms her brother's death was policy, not accident. Beat: the enemy defecting through evidence.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Three-way standoff: relay warming up, truce expiring, and a second fleet vessel inbound carrying the original order's author—Admiral Sennet, whose signature is all through the genome files. Beat: rising dread, every clock converging.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Begins
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Upload starts, but the relay needs continuous manual calibration; each correction costs minutes they don't have. Dario volunteers for the core ring without asking permission. Beat: love expressed as logistics.

chapters.title: Admiral Sennet Arrives
chapters.summary: Sennet's POV. Cold, reasonable, offering Mirabel amnesty and a restored colony contract if she kills the broadcast. He genuinely believes abandonment saved the many. Beat: evil as competent bookkeeping.

chapters.title: What Inheritance Costs
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She refuses—not with a speech but by handing Sennet the manifest with his own future date on it. The network marks judges, not just criminals. Sennet orders the relay destroyed anyway. Beat: quiet defiance meeting overwhelming force.

chapters.title: Hold the Line Open
chapters.summary: Dario's POV, climax part one. In the core ring, Dario calibrates by hand as weapons fire breaches the hull, keeping the channel alive with seconds of signal integrity left. Reyes turns her guns on Sennet's ship. Beat: sacrifice made concrete, minute by minute.

chapters.title: The Truth Goes Out
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax part two. The testimony completes its broadcast to every listening colony as the relay's core ring fails with Dario inside. His final transmission is simply her daily log format—one more entry, signed. Beat: devastation transfigured into continuity.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Silence
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Sennet retreats rather than become the next marked name; the truce collapses around him instead of them. Reyes gives Mirabel Dario's effects and chooses exile over return. Beat: survivors taking inventory of what remains.

chapters.title: One More Entry
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Back at the vault, she plants the first seed in open ground—the vault's purpose finally fulfilled—and records entry 4,001, addressed not to the fleet but to whoever inherits next. Beat: mourning folded into stewardship.

chapters.title: A Gravity for the Echo
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, coda. Years later, ships arrive answering the broadcast—colonists, witnesses, the children of the abandoned. Among the new manifests, a familiar name appears again, dated forward. She smiles, and keeps recording. Beat: hope as an inherited duty.
